messages:
alex: thinking out loud — proposal to add tiny per-prefix `lease_tag` (uint32) to make evictions and ownership handoffs deterministic and safe across concurrent transfers. idea: tag changes on every ownership transfer, compare-and-claim on evict/read paths. avoids relying purely on epoch/lease windows and reduces hairy race fallout.

ryan: quick q — how is this materially different from our epochs/leases? isn't this just another epoch field?

alex: good question. epochs are global-ish and we already have multi-layer leases. `lease_tag` is minimal (4 bytes) attached to prefix metadata and travels with ownership handoffs. difference: it's intended for fast local checks (evict/claim) and cheap reconciliation rather than long-lived coordination. think: a cheap monotonic tag that both old and new owner can use to validate residency during overlapping windows.

cheng: ok but memory/footprint concern — we have millions of prefixes. storing 4 bytes each is non-zero. where do you plan to store it? in the hot KV slab?

alex: plan A: store in the existing prefix metadata compact struct (we already store owner id + generation). this is an extra 4 bytes plus atomic update path on handoff. Plan B (fallback): store sparse tags in a small LRU side-table for prefixes that actually move frequently (hot movers).

maria: we should decide telemetry now: how will we know it's working / not regressing correctness? metric ideas: `lease_tag_mismatch_total`, `lease_tag_claim_latency_ms`, `evict_skips_due_to_tag_total`. also add small histogram for tag churn per-prefix.

sophia: ops nuance — tombstones + long cursors could observe stale tags. how do we avoid read-after-write regressions when a client resumes a long cursor right after a handoff?

alex: two-part: (1) on read path we check (owner == local && tag == expected) to accept fast path; if mismatch we fallback to authoritative directory read which is the current behavior. (2) for long cursors we add an optional `cursor_tag` that the client carries; server will detect mismatch and return an explicit `RESUME_RETRY` so clients can re-resolve. backwards compatible because existing clients ignore the field.

ryan: sounds ok. what's the claim protocol? any proto sketch?

alex: sketch: 
```proto
message LeaseTagClaim {
  string prefix = 1;
  uint32 expected_tag = 2; // 0 means no expectation (force claim)
  uint32 new_tag = 3;
  string claimant_node = 4;
}

// Server-side: atomically: if stored_tag == expected_tag then stored_tag = new_tag; return success/old_tag
```

cheng: atomically is the hard bit across replicas. we need to ensure our local metadata update is idempotent and persisted before we advertise ownership. otherwise we'll have a window where directory points to new owner but tag didn't persist and evictions race.

alex: agreed. handoff sequence idea: (1) claimant requests pre-claim, (2) owner prepares by writing new_tag and persisting locally, (3) owner ack, (4) directory update (atomic CAS on directory), (5) claimant completes claim and starts serving. this is similar to current lease handoff but swaps in `tag` persistence as a first-class step.

maria: migration plan? need off switches and incremental rollout.

alex: rollout proposal: opt-in config `lease_tag_enable=true`. start with small canary pool (1% tenants) for 48h, observe tag_mismatch_total and evict_skips. Then widen. Also provide a runtime flag to fallback to legacy path if any canary fails.

cheng: testing: add unit tests for atomic tag claim, chaos test that kills owner just after writing tag but before directory update, and integration that exercises long cursor resume. also add an automated invariant checker that scans prefix metadata for tag gaps.

ryan: what about eviction policy semantics? do tags change evict order?

alex: tags only protect correctness, not hotness. eviction still driven by score. `evict` will check tag to avoid evicting a prefix that is in a handoff window and thus still logically owned. If tag mismatch, evict returns `TRY_LATER` and increments `evict_skips_due_to_tag_total`.

sophia: ops: we need playbook entries for when `evict_skips` spikes — is it a permanent stall or transient?

maria: add alert: `evict_skips_rate > X` for Y minutes -> page oncall. but keep threshold high for canary. also make the skip counter sample per-prefix to avoid noise.

deploy-bot: canary run triggered: https://ci.internal/canaries/lease-tag-canary/1819998888 (status: queued)

cheng: compatibility note: older nodes that don't understand tags should behave ok because we fallback to authoritative directory on mismatch. but make sure directory updates are backward compatible (no extra fields breaking CAS).

alex: ownership: i'll own the RFC + prototype, cheng will own tests + chaos harness, maria will own metrics/alerts. I'll draft RFC today and link here.

maria: :thumbsup: please include expected telemetry dashboards and a short migration checklist in the RFC.

alex: will do. next steps: RFC by EOD, prototype PR targeting a feature-flag branch, small canary next week. tagging stakeholders: @ryan @cheng @maria for review.
